What Questions Should I Ask Before Hiring a Landscaper?

Hiring a landscaping company is an investment in your home, and choosing the right contractor can make all the difference. A well-designed and properly installed landscape should provide years of beauty and enjoyment, while poor workmanship can lead to costly repairs and ongoing frustration.

Before signing a contract, it’s important to ask the right questions. Doing so will help you find a qualified professional who understands your vision and can deliver lasting results.

Here are some of the most important questions every homeowner should ask before hiring a landscaper.

1. Are You Licensed and Insured?

This should always be your first question.

A reputable landscaping company should carry the appropriate licenses (when required) and have both liability insurance and workers’ compensation coverage.

This protects both you and the contractor if an accident or property damage occurs during the project.

2. How Much Experience Do You Have?

Experience matters.

Ask how long the company has been in business and whether they have experience with projects similar to yours.

Whether you’re planning a paver patio, landscape renovation, irrigation system, or outdoor lighting installation, you want a team that has successfully completed similar work before.

3. Can I See Examples of Your Work?

Photos of completed projects can tell you a lot about a company’s craftsmanship and design style.

Ask to see:

  • Before-and-after photos
  • Recent completed projects
  • Projects similar to yours
  • Different design styles

A professional landscaper should be proud to showcase their work.

4. Do You Have Customer Reviews or References?

Online reviews provide valuable insight into a company’s professionalism, communication, and quality of work.

Look for comments about:

  • Reliability
  • Communication
  • Timeliness
  • Attention to detail
  • Problem-solving
  • Overall customer satisfaction

You can also ask for references from previous clients if you’d like additional peace of mind.

5. What Is Included in the Estimate?

Not all estimates are created equal.

A detailed proposal should clearly outline:

  • Scope of work
  • Materials being used
  • Labor
  • Timeline
  • Payment schedule
  • Warranty information
  • Any exclusions or optional upgrades

Understanding exactly what’s included helps prevent surprises later.

6. Who Will Be Managing My Project?

It’s helpful to know who your primary point of contact will be throughout the project.

Ask:

  • Who supervises the crew?
  • How will updates be communicated?
  • Who should I contact with questions?
  • How are unexpected issues handled?

Clear communication is one of the keys to a successful landscaping project.

7. What Is the Expected Timeline?

Every project is different, but your landscaper should be able to provide a realistic timeline.

Be sure to ask:

  • When can the project begin?
  • How long will it take?
  • What factors could cause delays?
  • How will weather affect the schedule?

Setting expectations early helps everyone stay on the same page.

8. What Warranty Do You Offer?

A quality landscaping company stands behind its work.

Ask about warranties for:

  • Plant installations
  • Hardscape workmanship
  • Irrigation systems
  • Landscape lighting
  • Materials

Knowing what is covered provides added confidence in your investment.

9. Will My Landscape Require Ongoing Maintenance?

Some landscapes require much more maintenance than others.

Ask whether your design will need:

  • Regular pruning
  • Seasonal mulch
  • Fertilization
  • Irrigation adjustments
  • Weed control
  • Lawn maintenance

A good landscaper will recommend solutions that match both your lifestyle and maintenance preferences.

10. Why Should I Choose Your Company?

Finally, don’t be afraid to ask what sets one company apart from another.

The answer should go beyond price.

Look for a company that emphasizes:

  • Quality workmanship
  • Experienced professionals
  • Strong communication
  • Reliable service
  • Attention to detail
  • Long-term customer relationships

The best landscaper isn’t always the lowest bidder; it’s the one who provides the greatest value and delivers on their promises.

Red Flags to Watch For

While interviewing landscaping companies, keep an eye out for warning signs.

These may include:

  • Extremely low bids that seem too good to be true
  • Vague or incomplete estimates
  • No proof of insurance
  • Requests for full payment upfront
  • Poor communication or slow responses
  • Few or no customer reviews

Taking the time to research your contractor can save you significant time, money, and stress later.

The Bottom Line

Hiring a landscaper is about more than finding someone who can plant shrubs or install a patio; it’s about choosing a trusted partner who will help bring your vision to life.

By asking the right questions, reviewing past work, and choosing a company with a strong reputation, you’ll be well on your way to creating an outdoor space you can enjoy for years to come.
